attribution: CIE 2019, Colour-matching functions of CIE 1931 standard colorimetric observer, International Commission on Illumination (CIE), Vienna, AT, DOI:10.25039/CIE.DS.xvudnb9b. Adapted by 0sfs into absolute Planck/CIE emission tables with documented material and gas hypotheses.
rgbMeaning: Dimensional gray gas: source RGB cd/m3 and absorption m^-1; gray-particle LTE emission uses absolute Planck/CIE table, with independently bounded excited-band radiant watts. Solid RGB cd/m2 retains photopic Y after gamut clipping. PNG is an archival 10000 cd/m2 fixed-reference preview only, never runtime gas input. Runtime integrates transfer before explicit cd/m2 display reference and shared image processing.
uvMeaning: Only spatial PNG is sampled at runtime. R annular density, G downstream filled density; (1-z)^2 axial density and contracting radius 1-0.6z. Absolute gas/solid spectral tables are CPU interpolation data.
assumptions: Native gas K and separate native solid K retain separate physical meaning. No N1/N2-to-temperature conversion, color ramp, startup fade or render-time heat integrator exists. Gas and solid temperatures and material/particle inputs remain not measured F135 quantities.

The gas reduced transfer equation is dL_lambda/ds = j_lambda - kappa L_lambda, with gray particle j_lambda=kappa B_lambda(T) and independent optional excited-species emission. kappa has units m^-1, B_lambda is W sr^-1 m^-3, and the runtime integrated RGB Y is cd/m2 before display scaling. Scattering, line absorption and non-gray soot optics are not solved.

Particles are assumed isothermal with the native downstream gas bath. A stationary dimensionless annular particle-density field, contracting radius 1-0.6z and axial density (1-z)^2 describes a support volume, not CFD. Expensive mask and volume integrals are baked offline. Angular count 8 remains a provisional F-35A appearance hypothesis, not component, injector or light counts.

The absorption coefficients 0.025/m dry and 0.08/m AB are unmeasured gray particle loading hypotheses. Sensitivity covers 0..0.3/m. Across 1 m homogeneous path they imply optical depths 0.025/0.08 before density variation and fuel-budget caps; temperature alone does not fix opacity or particle loading.

Unattenuated bolometric particle source power is bounded by 4*kappa*sigma*T^4*integral(density dV). Effective kappa is reduced when that source exceeds the declared fraction of actual total fuel mass flow times 43.3 MJ/kg LHV. Particle power caps 0.3% dry/1.5% AB are conservative optical allocations, not measured radiation efficiencies or solved engine energy accounting.

Excited CH*/C2* band shapes have unit integrated visible radiant energy. Their retained amplitude is explicit visible watts = fraction*actual burned AB fuel kg/s*LHV, gated only by genuine augmentation and source availability. Missing/invalid burned-AB fuel gives zero bands. Default fraction 1e-6, sensitivity 0..1e-4, and equal band-energy weights are uncertainty hypotheses, not population measurements. No dry radical source is assumed. This is not a unique computed F135 color.

Actual fuel flow bounds the optical energy source; missing/invalid fuel suppresses gas. No optical power is subtracted from native gas/solid reservoirs, which are externally imposed inputs. The source-power upper bound includes photons subsequently reabsorbed; escaped power is no greater. Local bounds do not establish global energy conservation or close fuel, exhaust enthalpy, walls and radiation together.

Absolute Planck/CIE continuum tables retain cold radiance; no spectral/RGB peak normalization is used for runtime gas or solids. Log interpolation of positive gas channels avoids cold-to-hot amplification; zero gamut-clipped channels use linear interpolation. Out-of-range/invalid gas temperature is rejected rather than extrapolated. Spectral clipping preserves photopic Y.

Hot metal uses visible gray emissivity 0.8, with uncertainty range 0.3..0.95 pending alloy/coating/oxidation measurements. The same provisional spectrum is assigned to the two distinct material regions, each driven by its own native temperature. Visible emissivity is not substituted for native bolometric heat-loss emissivity. Planck solids do not develop a purple high-temperature ramp.

Gas and solid luminance have independent explicit cd/m2 display references. Shared scene exposure, tone mapping, curves/grading and encoding apply once. The transfer calculation is linear; exact radiance addition/absorption over the rendered background requires shared linear HDR postprocessing. Material-local display-space composition remains a renderer approximation, not an energy-conservation result.

One optional unshadowed point light uses the source-volume integral in candela, an upper-bound isotropic far-field approximation that omits plume self-absorption and near-field geometry. A dimensionless display gain defaults 1. It excludes the emitting engine meshes to avoid tinting its own cold hardware. Unlit raster terrain cannot receive it. Gas, solid, environmental reflection and nearby-light isolation are diagnostics, not separate physical energy sources.

Warm night powered-lift and pink/violet test-cell observations remain qualitative constraints with unknown camera response. Band population sensitivities can produce violet, but there is no forced warm-nozzle/purple-tail mixture schedule. The reported startup transition was not captured with native state; prior AB bank switching plus normalized band-rich spectrum and scene-light reflection are plausible contributors, not an established diagnosis.

sources.title: NIST, Realization of the candela
sources.supports: The photometric conversion integrates spectral radiance with the photopic observer and luminous efficacy factor. This supports luminance units and conversion, not an F135 visible emissivity or renderer exposure.

sources.title: NIST, Spectroradiometry of sources
sources.supports: Planck spectral radiance is the physical blackbody reference. An assumed visible-grey emissivity scales the hardware table; it does not establish the actual F135 wall temperature or spectral emissivity.

sources.title: NASA-TM-X-2711, Comparison of primary zone combustor liner wall temperatures with calculated predictions
sources.supports: A main-combustor liner experiment supports separate radiative/convective heat balance and film cooling. It is not an afterburner-liner study and supplies no F135 downstream metal temperatures or calibrated coefficients.

sources.title: NASA Kennedy Space Center, Thermography, Technique AT-9
sources.supports: Page 2 explains surface thermal radiation and visible emission from sufficiently hot solids. It supports a heated-hardware glow mechanism, not F135 nozzle temperatures or display brightness.

sources.title: 56th Fighter Wing, U.S. Marine Corps F-35B performs during Luke Days 2026
sources.supports: The caption identifies actual F-35B afterburner use; the daylight photograph shows warm visible emission. It is a qualitative representative reference, not a spectral calibration or universal hue.

sources.title: NASA/TM-2013-217884, Comparing a Fischer-Tropsch Alternate Fuel to JP-8 and Their 50-50 Blend
sources.supports: Section 4.1 describes CH* near 432 nm, C2* near 473/516/573 nm and soot-associated orange emission in jet-fuel combustor imaging. This supplies band locations and mechanisms, not F135 afterburner weights.

sources.title: NISTIR 6783, Fire Dynamics Simulator Technical Reference Guide
sources.supports: Section 4 treats Planck emission, absorption and continuous soot radiation; it also warns that a grey approximation can overpredict optically thin emission. The simplified continuum here is an assumption.

sources.title: CIE 2019, Colour-matching functions of CIE 1931 standard colorimetric observer
sources.supports: Official 1 nm observer functions used to integrate the assumed emission spectrum into XYZ.

sources.title: Retained F-35A rear-view sequence at 1:32
sources.supports: Qualitative uneven bright annulus and darker center. Eight lobes are unresolved; no B geometry or calibrated temperature inference. Retained frame in validation/evidence/aircraft/f35b/engine-review-2026-10-06/frames/rear-92.png.

sources.title: Royal Navy powered-lift night footage via Navy Lookout
sources.supports: External red/orange exhaust-region emission and deck illumination. Species, staging telemetry, exposure and white balance unavailable; operational hover AB remains inhibited.

sources.title: P&W-sponsored F135 factory and test-cell video
sources.supports: Pink/violet photographed plume exists. Does not prove a universal spectrum or identify B-specific calibrated optical mixture.
